A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spectral-Refiner research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across renaming, relocation and expansion.

before.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2, Tables 1–3 and Appendix D report original neural-operator training and fine-tuning results for Taylor-Green vortex and turbulent-flow simulations.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and adds runtime measurements, spectral analyses and out-of-distribution turbulence evaluations, including unsuccessful fine-tuning.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the stated lifting operator from pointwise projection after time-depth convolution to a construction using projected positional encodings and learnable layer normalization. The central final-layer spectral fine-tuning procedure, negative-Sobolev loss and solver-derived time derivatives remain intact. Renaming SFNO to ST-FNO is not itself a method change.

E1.justification: The original flow benchmarks remain, while Appendix D.4 adds evaluations with shifted initial-energy concentrations k0 = 2 and 8 and Reynolds numbers 5000 and 10000, substantially extending tested flow conditions. Appendix C.3 also changes the reported Example II forcing from mid-wavenumber forcing to no external force.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 remove their FNO3d baseline rows, and Table 3 removes FNO3d trained with the H−1 loss. New Table 6 evaluates FNO3d rollout and IMEX Runge-Kutta comparators, while Figure 13 introduces FNO(2+1)d rollout. These materially change comparator membership within the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Added experiments use 15-epoch models, 512×512 or 1024×1024 evaluation grids, prediction-step correlation measurements and controlled timing protocols with specified horizons and sampling intervals. Appendix C.3 newly specifies RK4/implicit-Euler data generation, conflicting with the second-order description retained in Section 4.2. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained loss ablations, v2 adds distribution-shift and high-Reynolds-number robustness tests, a nonperiodic-padding comparison in Figure 7, and a prediction/fine-tuning case study in Figure 12. The earlier spectrum analysis is expanded into comparisons across training epochs, trajectories and time points in Figures 8–9.

E5.justification: V1 already reports fixed-seed training and a ten-seed spectrum experiment. V2 specifies seed 1127825, introduces mean-centered error bars of ±10 standard deviations in Figure 8, and reports runtime averages with ± values over 20 runs in Table 6. The runtime dispersion statistic is unspecified; increased training replication is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 and the new figures add timing, correlation and shifted-distribution results, including a post-fine-tuning L2 error of 2.355×10^6 in the Re = 10000 case. Table 3 changes reported FNO3d L2 errors from 0.0244 to 0.0432 at 10 epochs and from 0.0432 to 0.0387 at 100 epochs. Corresponding proposed-method numbers in Tables 1–3 are retained; the added evaluations are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The principal residual bounds, norm-equivalence proof and local-convexity results are retained. Appendix B adds a Poisson-operator boundedness/stability argument for H−1 residual measurement, and the final convergence argument now specifies a linearly converging step size. The Pythagorean identity is relocated to Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: V1 presents a specific SFNO architecture and limits applicability to non-factorized FNO. V2 claims an adaptation for any FNO variant, explicitly including factorized FNO, and newly promotes convex fine-tuning in the abstract and introduction. It also qualifies advantages over numerical solvers with 'under certain conditions'; the central hybrid-learning and large accuracy-improvement claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains padding's role in suppressing nonperiodic endpoint artifacts and reinterprets the McWilliams enstrophy spectrum as a k−3 direct cascade rather than the inverse cascade described in v1. It also acknowledges unsuccessful fine-tuning in the highest-Reynolds-number shifted scenario, adding an empirical applicability limit to the existing conditional-convergence caveats.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds substantial reproduction information: generation grids, time steps, downsampling, warmup, 1024 training trajectories and training/testing snapshot construction. Appendix D.3 supplies the fine-tuning learning rate, and Table 6 specifies timing hardware and power controls. Conversely, Table 5 removes Taylor-Green model-size and mode details. Public code and data access already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds comparisons with Bayesian residual correction, distinguishes the H−1 loss from Du et al.'s L2 spectral loss, and incorporates recent Transformer and state-space operator work. Some design-inspiration references, including ConvNeXt, are removed. These extend the existing research positioning without replacing its central operator-learning and numerical-analysis framework.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten and reorganizes motivations and contributions. Architecture and hybrid training become separate Sections 2 and 3, while mathematical and de-aliasing motivation moves to Appendix B. The title and SFNO/ST-FNO terminology change, and the lifting, projection and temporal-super-resolution explanations are substantially expanded.

P2.justification: V2 adds architecture diagrams, padding and shifted-flow visualizations, correlation plots, and runtime and robustness tables. The old spectrum figure is replaced and expanded, while v1 Figures 2–4 largely reappear as v2 Figures 4–6. Tables 1–2 become compact side-by-side displays, and the document adopts a substantially revised conference layout.

improvement.justification: The added generation details, timing evidence and shifted-distribution tests make the study easier to reproduce and its practical limits easier to assess, including a clearly reported failure. These gains are tempered by removed baseline comparisons and broader claims: applicability across FNO variants is not tested across architectures, and the new unqualified convexity claim is supported only by the retained local-convexity theory in Lemma E.8.
